items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: He said, "Well, play a B-flat chord and just keep playing the chord over and over." And he played this solo.

ctx.x: anything in B-flat?" -- because he wanted to show off this solo that he'd learned. I said, "Oh, no, I can't play anything." He said, "Do you know a B-flat chord?" I said, "Oh yeah." He said, "Well, play a B-flat chord and just keep playing the chord over and over." And he played this solo. When he got to the bridge, which went through a D-seven and a G-seven, a C-seven, F, he said "Just lay out there; don't play anything there." And after he finished the bridge, I came back and played some more B-flat.

So after that particular night, I hurried home, and the next day I was up early learning this particular tune in B-flat, which was a very easy transposition to make -- although I didn't know it at that particular time. And that next night I went back, I was ready for him!
